evidence.observation: A close-up shows a relatively thick-bodied, dark fish angled diagonally head-upper-left to tail-lower-right, with a gently curved belly and a lighter patch near the head/gill.
evidence.distinguishes_because: This robust diagonal shape matches Y at 0.0 (I002 bbox [0.5,0.9,1.0,1.0]) better than the slimmer, more vertical X at 0.0, favoring C1? No, favoring C2 (Y=A).

evidence.observation: B's last close-up before time 0 is a slimmer fish in a more vertical pose, with a narrower body profile than A.
evidence.distinguishes_because: X at 0.0 (I002 bbox [0.5,0.6,1.0,0.7]) shares this slim, more vertical shape, whereas Y at 0.0 is thicker/diagonal like A, supporting X=B and thus C2.

evidence.observation: In the separate time-0 composite, X's close-up is again the slimmer, more vertical fish, while the adjacent Y close-up is the larger, diagonally oriented fish.
evidence.distinguishes_because: This independently pairs X with the B-like shape and Y with the A-like shape at the last supplied time, supporting C2 (X=B, Y=A) rather than C1.

decision.limitation: The comparison relies on visual similarity of close-up body shape and orientation; A has only one earlier frame and there is a large temporal gap, so this is not a numerical proof.
